problems.title: Dimension reduction cannot preserve all source geometry
claim: The text invokes rotational invariance after truncating a square orthogonal matrix to align a lower-dimensional teacher, attributing feature-shape preservation to that map.
analysis: In a favorable orientation let \(A=Q_d^{\top}\), \(AA^{\top}=I_d\), \(P=A^{\top}A\). Then \(\|Av\|^2=\|v\|^2-\|(I-P)v\|^2\). With \(D=4,d=2,Q=\exp(0)=I_4\), the projection retains only the first two coordinates: \(e_3,e_4\) collapse to zero despite distance \(\sqrt2\). The data matrix containing the standard basis has full row rank, so a full-rank assumption does not rescue preservation. Multiplication by any fixed projection remains linear regardless of sample count/rank.
result: Norms/distances survive exactly on retained directions, not all source features. Tensor-dimension alignment and possible task-relevant approximate preservation remain intact.
repair: State contraction and retained-subspace isometry. If discarded pairwise components are at most \(\varepsilon\) times original distance, retained distance lies between \(\sqrt{1-\varepsilon^2}\) and one times original distance; that data-dependent condition is not established here.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded correction to a geometric explanation, without proof of lost useful information in learned data.

problems.title: Separate orthogonality does not eliminate shared-gradient conflicts
claim: Per-map identities \(A_iA_i^{\top}=I\) do not control cross-map inner products \(g_i^{\top}g_j=r_i^{\top}A_iA_j^{\top}r_j\).
analysis: Use coordinate projections from \(\mathbb R^4\) retaining first \(2\) and first \(3\) coordinates, both permitted truncations of \(I_4\). At \(z=(1,1,1,0)\), apply softmax to projected features and use teachers \((0.9,0.1)\), \((0.1,0.8,0.1)\). For teacher-to-student KL, shared gradients are \((-2/5,2/5,0,0)\) and \((7/30,-7/15,7/30,0)\), inner product \(-7/25<0\). For the printed reversed KL direction it is \(-\log9\log8/12<0\). Thus improving one term can worsen the other to first order under either convention. Softmax is an explicit favorable domain assumption, not recovered unavailable code.
result: Individual projection orthogonality permits this operational conflict. Conditioning improvements, learned conflict reduction and empirical benefit remain possible; no universal parameter-gradient result follows.
repair: Describe a per-projection constraint and empirical regularizer; measure defined gradient conflicts. Cross-map orthogonality would suffice at the shared-feature level but is not imposed and may be infeasible; it is not offered as a validated replacement.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The counterexample removes a blanket explanatory guarantee while leaving dimensional alignment and unrerun accuracy results intact.
